item.description:
School District of Lancaster students and families are invited to an evening of hands-on math fun at the SDoL Math Fair on Wednesday, Oct. 28, from 5:30-7 p.m. at Wickersham Elementary. Hosted in partnership with Mathematics Educators at Millersville University, the district-wide event is designed for students in K through 5th grade to explore math through interactive games and activities while building their skills and confidence. item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Oct 28, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: White House Workers — Thu Oct 29, 5:30 PM — LancasterHistory
item.description:
Join White House Historical Association historian Sarah Fling as she highlights lesser-known stories of White House workers throughout history, including the men and women who worked for President James Buchanan.
Sarah Fling is a historian at the White House Historical Association. Her research focuses on free and enslaved workers, the first ladies, and the White House Collection. Fling is a contributor in The Cambridge Companion to US First Ladies (2025) and has published her research in White House History Quarterly and Teen Vogue. She serves on the Board of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, and previously served as a Community Lead in the Youth250 Bureau, a non-partisan initiative that highlighted the Gen Z perspective during America’s 250th. Sarah’s previous work experience includes internships at historic sites such as George Washington’s Mount Vernon and the Frick Pittsburgh. She received her bachelor’s degree in History from the University of Pittsburgh

item.title: Anti-Fascist Craft Night in Lititz with the Warwick Democrats! — Wed Nov 4, 3:00 PM — Lititz
item.description:
We love democracy. We love crafts. We love civic engagement. Why not combine them?! Join us for **Anti-Fascist Craft Night** in Lititz—a low-key hang where we make wild collage postcards and letters to send our thoughts (and shade) to our elected officials, design signs for the next protest, . Make your voice heard in a weirdly therapeutic and hands-on way! **What to bring:** * Clean cardboard (cereal/snack boxes) or card stock * Old magazines, catalogs, newspapers, greeting cards, etc. * Scisso
Source: Lancaster County Dems (Mobilize)

item.title: Trivia Night at Southern Market - Meet People Lancaster team — Wed Nov 11, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Meet People Lancaster Do you love trivia nights, but want to avoid the hassle of trying to wrangle up enough friends to field a team? Come play for a Meet People Lancaster team and make some new friends along the way! Cost: FREE Bar & food stations are all walk up. You’ll be on your own tab for the night. Host: Elizabeth Chapman Please try to get there by 6:30PM, so we can get situated at a couple tables. Trivia starts at 7PM. If you come early, you’ll have time to mingle and get some food before trivia starts.
Location: 100 S Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603 How to find the group: Our “usual” trivia spot is the tables in front of Gloomy Rooster/Noodle King in the front left corner. We will also have a few yellow MPL signs!
Source: Meetup: Meet People Lancaster
